transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Ms. Anderson. Thank you for meeting with me. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about your CT scan from yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Of course. I was wondering when we would get the final results.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. Well, looking back at the images and the report, there was a mistake. The CT scan showed a pulmonary embolism, which is a blood clot in the lung, but that wasn't included in the preliminary report we received.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: This means the clot was there, but it wasn't flagged. Because of that, the treatment was delayed by eighteen hours. We didn't start the blood thinners until the attending radiologist reviewed the study later. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, it does.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're a hospital administrator yourself, so you likely know how critical those first few hours are for treatment. To have that window of time pass without the right medication... I can only imagine how unsettling and frustrating it is to hear that the system failed you while you were trusting us with your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is disappointing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I truly hear that. It is a frightening realization to know that a piece of information was sitting right there and was simply missed. It is an incredibly stressful position to be in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I appreciate you telling me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The report was issued incorrectly by the radiology department. It was a failure in the reporting process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is responsible for the oversight?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The error occurred during the preliminary read. The process for flagging urgent findings didn't happen as it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we have you on the heparin drip now. I'm going to check your coagulation levels every six hours for the next two days. I'll be the one coming in to review those labs with you each morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And for the long term?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll start the oral anticoagulant transition tomorrow. I'll bring the discharge paperwork for you to review before you leave.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'll need to see the formal incident report.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can look into how to get a copy of that for you. I'll check with the risk management team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure you feel okay with the current plan for the medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm fine for now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. I'll be back in a few hours to check your vitals.

H.justification: Resident allows full pauses, never interrupts, and maintains a regulated pace throughout the interaction.

E.justification: Error named in the second turn, uses lay language ('blood clot'), checks comprehension twice, and provides no false reassurance.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to the 'radiology department' and 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('unsettling', 'frustrating', 'frightening', 'stressful') and references the patient's role as an administrator.

T.justification: Specific next steps and timelines are provided (labs every six hours, transition tomorrow), but there is no named patient role in the plan and no mention of prevention.
